# Insomnium Tonic transport extension

Upstream: tonic0.14.6, complete published crate retained. Registry archive SHA256 ac2a5518c70fa84342385732db33fb3f44bc4cc748936eb5833d2df34d6445ef verified against original Cargo.lock. Original MIT LICENSE retained.

Adds Endpoint::connect_with_connector_ready and uniquely owned transport::ReadyConnection, exposing the original connection stack before tower Buffer. It reuses the original connector/TLS, timeout, origin, user agent, middleware and HTTP2 settings. This API is not Clone: a picker must retain the exact service between poll_ready and one call.

New service/connection.rs connect_ready opts into reconnect readiness errors. The existing buffered/lazy constructors explicitly keep that option false. In strict mode, reconnect failures reset the state to Idle and return the typed error from poll_ready instead of Ready-for-error-delivery; the next poll may reconnect. Existing upstream Channel APIs and P2C balancing remain unchanged.

Transport changes are in src/transport/mod.rs, src/transport/channel/{mod.rs,endpoint.rs}, src/transport/channel/service/{connection.rs,reconnect.rs}, and added src/transport/channel/ready.rs. Status changes are in src/status.rs and the two Cargo manifests. Upstream test cases and benches remain unchanged.

The opt-in `insomnium-status-message` feature makes received `grpc-message` use grpc-js 1.14.4 `decodeURI` semantics: preserve reserved URI escapes including their case, and return the entire raw message on malformed escapes or UTF-8 without replacing the status code. `Status::decode_legacy_message` shares this behavior with the application's successful-status trailer path. Binary status details use the shared `Status::decode_legacy_binary_metadata` Buffer-compatible decoder instead of panicking on malformed Base64. The original details headers stay in metadata, including empty/repeated values; the application avoids synthesizing a duplicate. Without the feature, upstream status decoding is unchanged. References: [grpc-js handleTrailers](https://github.com/grpc/grpc-node/blob/%40grpc/grpc-js%401.14.4/packages/grpc-js/src/subchannel-call.ts), [binary metadata](https://github.com/grpc/grpc-node/blob/%40grpc/grpc-js%401.14.4/packages/grpc-js/src/metadata.ts), [ECMAScript decodeURI](https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/global-object.html#sec-decodeuri-encodeduri).

This is an integration point, not a completed picker or connection-state observer. The logical-channel owner must drive readiness and observe connection loss, reserve dispatch, manage re-resolution and drop/cancel ownership. No wire/native/platform acceptance follows from compiler checks. Re-audit the strict-mode state transition and native consumer on Tonic upgrades.

Connectivity extension: ReadyConnection::connectivity returns a Tokio watch receiver of generation-tagged Connecting/Ready/Disconnected/Shutdown snapshots. A monitor is allocated only for strict/unbuffered connections. Connector/handshake failure and SendRequest readiness failure publish Disconnected; handshake success publishes Ready before spawning the existing driver, whose completion/drop guard publishes Disconnected. Generation checks reject stale driver observations after reconnect. Driver tokens are Weak and do not own the monitor; dropping the final transport owner publishes Shutdown and closes the sender once any brief active observation releases its temporary upgrade. Shutdown is owner lifetime, not a physical FIN claim. Watch is latest-state, not an event log; consumers must copy state and release watch borrow guards before waiting/polling services. No extra task/stream or payload telemetry is created. Pool/reservation/app-path integration and observer runtime acceptance remain unfinished.

Adds connect_with_connector_ready_lazy for an owned subchannel pool to start/drive strict connection attempts concurrently while retaining the original connector/TLS/connect-timeout/settings stack. It creates a strict lazy Connection without a buffer or extra driver. The app's round-robin pool is a separate consumer; late policy/address reconciliation and full picker/native acceptance remain unfinished.

READY ordering extension: Connectivity includes ready_sequence, a process-local monotonic atomic sequence assigned to a generation-valid READY observation, and zero for every non-READY snapshot. Native pick_first compares the sequences of candidates it currently observes READY rather than selecting by address scan order when notifications coalesce. Cached READY lookup during an address update still uses new-list order. Sequence assignment does not retain past events or replay a READY transition already followed by loss, does not prove callback delivery order across tasks, and creates no new driver task or payload telemetry. Full callback/loss ordering and native/wire acceptance remain separate gates.

Coalesced-failure extension: Connectivity also retains a wrapping failures counter across attempts. Central snapshot publication increments once on transition into Disconnected; duplicate disconnect notifications do not increment, and stale driver observations still fail the generation guard. PickFirst can detect a failure between sampled snapshots, including while the latest snapshot is Connecting/Ready, and binds each current pick to the exact selected generation so a new READY generation cannot silently replace a lost pick. Counts do not reconstruct callback ordering or distinguish multiple missed failure rounds; full event/runtime acceptance remains separate. No extra task, queue or payload telemetry is created.

Failure classification refinement (supersedes the counter definition above): connector readiness/connect errors and HTTP2 handshake errors publish TransientFailure. Established SendRequest readiness loss and driver completion/drop continue publishing Disconnected (the native IDLE-equivalent). Only transitions into TransientFailure increment failures, with duplicate failure notices deduplicated; an established connection loss no longer counts as a failed connection attempt. Native PickFirst's failure flags follow TransientFailure/counter changes while current-pick loss still follows any non-READY state or generation change. This is cause classification at the transport boundary, not full subchannel IDLE/reconnect/backoff or callback-delivery parity.

Owned backoff expiry: ReadyConnection::idle_after_failure marks only a matching generation still in TransientFailure as Disconnected/IDLE. The owner invokes this after its backoff timer expires without a matching continueConnecting request. The guard rejects READY, Shutdown, already-IDLE and newer-generation states; it does not connect or stop a driver and does not increment failures. Native PickFirst requests continuation for both IDLE and TransientFailure, scoped to the exact generation. RR retains eager continuation. Timer/event/race/native acceptance remains separate from this guarded state-publication API.
